subject: Re-run bench slice WITH #33 fixes + LLM-judge score → real before/after vs the pilot
description:
Measure whether the #33 fixes (date-in-body + full-text context + DAG+RAG injection) moved the score. Re-run the SAME slice as the #31 pilot — 3 LoCoMo convs (5 probes each) + 5 LongMemEval-S questions — through all 3 arms, reusing the downloaded data at C:\\Users\\Imyu\\.zonoid-bench-data, then SCORE with the LLM-judge (scorer.py) for real % per arm. Also re-score the pilot's old results.jsonl (on disk) with the same judge so the before/after is apples-to-apples.

CRITICAL HANG-AVOIDANCE: run in SHORT FOREGROUND CHUNKS — ONE conversation per Bash call (timeout ≤600000), NO run_in_background, NO poll loop. (The #31 pilot hung precisely because a subagent launched a background run and polled it, burning its turn budget.) ~8 convs = ~8 bounded foreground calls + a scoring call; the worker stays well within budget. Embedded daemon ORCH_HEADLESS_DRAINS=0; per claude -p ≤120s. Report our-way/search/cold accuracy per dataset, before (pilot) vs after (#33), with the per-probe deltas. Honesty bar: gold never in retrieve/keep/answer.
